description: A Unicode property class is refused by the baseline descriptor and by validation here.
descriptor: { descriptor_version: "1.0", root: { type: "object", children: { a: { type: "string", pattern: "\\p{L}" } } } }

divergence.note: docs/grammars.md §1.2 and §1.3 fix which layer reports each regex construct, and §1.2 states that the two implementations can name the same problem at different layers while the outcome (refused, named, never guessed at) does not differ. This is a documented, intentional divergence from the executed baseline under that rule (SPEC.md amendment 26), not a baseline defect.  The baseline `re` engine reads \p as a bad escape, so its descriptor compile check refuses the file; this engine compiles a real property class, so the dialect scan refuses it at validation as the docs §1.2 property-class row prescribes (the engines read the same text differently, which is why the row exists).
